dedupe_keys.name: kruibeke bazel rupelmonde controlled flood area sigma plan scheldt estuary

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Kruibeke Bazel Rupelmonde (KBR) controlled flood area, the largest water storage area of Belgium's Sigma Plan for the Scheldt Estuary, which was designed after the 1976 storm surge that broke a dike at Ruisbroek and forced over 2,000 people to evacuate. Former river dikes were lowered and new dikes built further inland, turning three contiguous polders of 600 hectares into an area that floods during storm tides, protecting about 20,000 hectares, while also restoring tidal and wetland habitats and offering recreation. Initiated in 1977, it came into operation in 2015, and nature restoration continued to 2018 under the EU LIFE SCALLUVIA project; it first proved its value in the strong tide of January 2018. The budget was about 100 million euros, three-quarters for studies and works and one-quarter for expropriation, across more than 100 contracts. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the Sigma Plan website. Caveats: long local opposition had to be overcome, and benefits are reported jointly with the wider Sigma Plan. It illustrates nature-based storm surge and flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation of estuary defences under sea level rise; related records are the Room for the River Regge and Isar-Plan case studies and the Global Flood Database.
name: Kruibeke Bazel Rupelmonde controlled flood area (Sigma Plan, Scheldt Estuary)
outcomes: The 600 ha controlled flood area operates since 2015, protects about 20,000 ha and buffered the strong tide of January 2018, preventing dangerous flooding.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the Sigma Plan
resources_used: Nature Management Plan of the Flemish government
